[[File:Hanno Mottola.jpg|thumb|Möttölä playing for Finland in 2008]]

'''Hanno Aleksanteri Möttölä''' (born 9 September 1976) is a Finnish professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is currently an assistant coach for the [[Brisbane Bullets]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah Utes]] before playing two seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] between 2000 and 2002, becoming the first player from Finland to play in the NBA.

==College career==
Möttölä attended the [[University of Utah]], in the United States, where he played [[college basketball]] under head coach [[Rick Majerus]]. He was a starter on the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah Utes]] team that played in the final of the [[1998 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1998 NCAA national championship tournament]], which they lost to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].

Möttölä was named in the Utah Athletics Hall of Fame in September 2023.<ref>[https://www.hnmky.fi/uutiset/julkaisu/10019 Namikakasvatti Hanno Möttölä valittiin Utahin yliopiston Hall of Fameen], hnmky.fi, 27 September 2023</ref>

==Professional career==
After college, Möttölä was selected in the second round, with the 40th overall pick, in the [[2000 NBA draft]], by the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He played two seasons in the [[NBA]] with the Hawks. He played in all 82 games during his sophomore (and final) season. His final NBA game was on April 17, 2002, in an 81–89 loss to the Boston Celtics where he recorded 1 steal and 2 rebounds.

After his time with the Hawks, he returned to [[Europe]] to play in the [[EuroLeague]]. He played in [[Spain]] with [[Saski Baskonia|TAU Cerámica]] of the [[Liga ACB]], where he suffered an ankle injury. Then he played in [[Italy]] with [[Fortitudo Bologna|Skipper Bologna]] (in the 2003–04 season, his team reached the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] finals and [[2004 EuroLeague Final Four|EuroLeague Final]]). He also played in Italy with [[Victoria Libertas Pesaro|Scavolini Pesaro]] (from 2004 to 2005).

Möttölä also played in the [[Russian Basketball Super League 1|Russian Super League]] with [[MBC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]], in the [[Lietuvos Krepšinio Lyga|Lithuanian LKL League]] with [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]], and in the [[Greek Basket League]] (GBL) with [[Aris BC|Aris]], after signing with the team on 26 July 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/14661/aris-inks-big-men-mottola-and-agadakos |title=Aris inks big men Mottola and Agadakos |last=Sotirou |first=Kostas |date=2007 |website=Euroleague |access-date= 5 February 2017}}</ref>

Möttölä announced his retirement from playing basketball on 26 September 2008,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=1846 |title=Hanno Mottola of Finland retires |website=Inside Hoops |access-date=5 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213165953/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=1846 |archive-date=13 February 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> but decided to return to basketball just nine months later.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.solobasket.com/liga-endesa/hanno-mottola-vuelve-las-canchas |title=Hanno Mottola vuelve a las canchas |last=Martinez |first=Frans |date=2009 |website= Solo Basket |access-date=5 February 2017 |language=es}}</ref> In September 2009, Möttölä signed with the Finnish team [[Torpan Pojat]]. He played in the team for four seasons, during which the team was the runner-up in the [[Korisliiga|Finnish League]] championship (2009–10), in the [[Finnish Basketball Cup|Finnish Cup]] (2010–11), and finished in third-place in Finnish League (2011–12).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.basket.fi/uutiset/?x22026=16400678  |title=Hanno Möttölä vahvistaa ToPoa Divisioona A:n kärjessä |website= Basket.fi |access-date=5 February 2017 |language=fi}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:EuroBasket 2017 Greece vs Finland 105.jpg|thumb|Möttölä at the [[EuroBasket 2017]]]]
Möttölä was a long-time member of the senior [[Finnish national basketball team]]. With Finland, he played at the [[1995 EuroBasket]], the [[2011 EuroBasket]], the [[2013 EuroBasket]], and the [[2014 FIBA World Cup]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140311/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/hanno%20mottola/pid//_//players.html Hanno MÖTTÖLÄ (FIN).]</ref>

==Coaching career==
After ending his playing career, Möttölä has worked as the head coach of Helsinki Basketball Academy team [[HBA-Märsky]] in second-tier [[Koripallon I-divisioona]], and an assistant coach of [[Finnish national basketball team|Finland national team]] since 2019.

In May 2024, Möttölä was invited to coach at [[NBA G League]] Elite Camp and at the 2024 [[NBA draft combine]] event.<ref>[https://www.itahame.fi/urheilu/6756195 Hanno Möttölä valmentajaksi NBA:n Draft Combine -leirille], Itä-Häme, 10 May 2024</ref><ref>[https://www.basket.fi/basket/uutiset/hanno-mottola-valmentajaksi-nba-draft-combine-leirille/ Hanno Möttölä valmentajaksi NBA Draft Combine -leirille], basket.fi, 10 May 2024</ref>

In August 2025, it was announced that Möttölä would join the coaching staff of the [[Canada men's national basketball team]] after the [[EuroBasket 2025]] tournament with Finland.<ref>[https://www.basket.fi/basket/uutiset/hanno-mottola-kanadan-maajoukkueen-valmennusjohtoon/ Hanno Möttölä Kanadan maajoukkueen valmennusjohtoon], basket.fi, 12 August 2025</ref>

In May 2026, Möttölä was appointed an assistant coach for the [[Brisbane Bullets]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL).<ref>{{cite news |title=Brisbane Bullets welcome Hanno Möttölä to coaching group {{!}} Brisbane Bullets |url=https://www.brisbanebullets.com.au/news/brisbane-bullets-welcome-hanno-mottola-to-coaching-group |access-date=26 May 2026 |work=www.brisbanebullets.com.au |date=26 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Finnish [[ice hockey]] players, [[Jarkko Ruutu]] and [[Tuomo Ruutu]], are Möttölä's second cousins.<ref>[http://www.ihanfinaalissa.fi/leijonat/8/tuomo-ruutu/ Tuomo Ruutu; ihanfinaalissa.fi] {{in lang|fi}}  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100210071016/http://www.ihanfinaalissa.fi/leijonat/8/tuomo-ruutu/ |date=2010-02-10 }}</ref>
